proposals.reason: One HTTP fixture boundary reuses existing session/client/native API fixture, admits document requests through public0.1.2, and returns canonical shared synthetic public fixtures. Its held-request helper observes the same request finishing or explicitly aborting before assertions; URL creation/revocation instrumentation is observation only. Keeping interception, response queue and request audit together makes effect isolation reviewable.

One parameterized complete document lifecycle scenario retains explicit user actions and their request/response assertions in order: no automatic request, create, inspect, verified byte download, acknowledged revision and resource disposal, plus native-limit captions, responsive captures and full default axe. The same scenario runs both supported families at desktop/phone sizes; all are genuine receiver/host paths. Phase splitting would disperse causal assertions and require extra fixture state.

One scenario follows the same uncertain or in-flight delivery across Modules navigation, Back/Forward, reconnect and a separately successful inspect. It asserts that the original write fence survives each transition and cannot be cleared by inspecting a version. The closure directly owns the held request and exact before/after call counts; no unrelated responsibilities or ambient sleeps.
